# Main current-account balance and overdraft use

Files: `balances_and_overdraft.pdf`, `balances_and_overdraft.svg` (this file: `balances_and_overdraft.md`), written by `ob_figures.py` (task T25).

**The data are synthetic.** They were generated by `ob_generator.py` from ONS averages (Family Spending, uprated), FCA Financial Lives 2024 holding rates and stated synthetic assumptions, so this figure describes the generator, not real customers.

## Source data

Source: the 100 files `Analysis/open_banking/persona*.json` (Open Banking Read/Write v3.1 objects; seed 20261107) and `Analysis/open_banking/ground_truth.csv`, written by `ob_generator.py` at commit `0aff08f`; read by `ob_figures.py` (commit `fcf62e6` or later). Plot style: `figstyle.py` (Auro's front-end style) sha256 `91e3bd61f98a`. No random numbers are drawn here (seed: not applicable).

## Filters, transformations and units

Main current account of each person (`AccountId` equal to the persona's uuid8; not the second, joint or card accounts). The balance
for each day is the running `Balance` after the day's last booked transaction (forward-filled over days without transactions,
starting from the `OpeningBooked` balance); pending transactions are excluded. Credit balances are positive, debit balances
negative. Left: median and interquartile range (25th to 75th percentile, linear interpolation) across the 100 persons, per day, 1 November 2025
to 31 October 2026. Right: for each month, the number of persons whose end-of-day balance was below zero on at least one day
("overdrawn"), and the number whose balance fell below minus their arranged overdraft limit (`overdraft_limit` in `ground_truth.csv`; "beyond arranged limit",
i.e. unarranged overdraft). The generator tops up an overdrawn account from savings at the end of each day where possible, so intraday dips are
not counted. Plotted data: [`Analysis/open_banking_figures/main_balance_daily.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/main_balance_daily.csv)
and [`overdraft_by_month.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/overdraft_by_month.csv).

## Statistics

Over the year 6 persons were overdrawn at the end of at least one day and 3 were beyond their arranged limit on at least one day.
The median balance moved from GBP 1,874.07 on 1 November 2025 to GBP 12,068.90 on 31 October 2026. No tests or
error bars (not applicable; quartiles describe the spread across persons).

## Interpretation

Typical balances grow over the year, because the generator does not model all ONS spending and holds pay and prices at 2026
levels; they are higher than real current accounts would be. Only a minority of persons (twelve) are ever overdrawn at a day end, and the five flagged in `ground_truth.csv` (committed payments above pay) account for the unarranged overdraft. This is a property of the synthetic assumptions, not of real customers.
